title: Qwen Developers Open-Sources zg (zvec-grep): A Local-First Search Layer Unifying ripgrep, BM25, and Vector Search
summary: We look at zg (zvec-grep), the local-first search layer that Qwen Developers just open-sourced under Apache 2.0. We explain how it puts ripgrep, BM25, and vector search behind a single interface, so an agent can move from a plain-language description to an exact line span without switching tools. We cover the deliberately small MCP surface, the on-device embedding catalog, and the authorization gate that stands between local content and remote models. The post Qwen Developers Open-Sources zg (zvec-grep): A Local-First Search Layer Unifying ripgrep, BM25, and Vector Search appeared first on MarkTechPost .

summary_zh: Qwen开发者开源zg，一个本地优先的搜索层，将ripgrep、BM25和向量搜索统一于单一接口，具备小型MCP表面、设备端嵌入和远程模型授权门。

title: Meet Switchyard: A Rust Proxy and Library That Routes and Translates LLM Traffic Across OpenAI and Anthropic APIs
summary: NVIDIA has released Switchyard, an Apache-2.0 Rust proxy and library for LLM traffic. It decodes requests into provider-neutral types, routes them with passthrough, random, LLM-classifier, or stage-router algorithms, and translates responses back into the client's format, so Claude Code or Codex CLI can run against vLLM, NIM, or Ollama unchanged. The project is pre-alpha and not for production. The post Meet Switchyard: A Rust Proxy and Library That Routes and Translates LLM Traffic Across OpenAI and Anthropic APIs appeared first on MarkTechPost .

summary_en: NVIDIA released Switchyard, an Apache-2.0 Rust proxy and library for LLM traffic. It decodes requests into provider-neutral types, routes them via multiple algorithms, and translates responses, enabling tools like Claude Code to run on vLLM or NIM. Pre-alpha, not for production.
summary_zh: NVIDIA发布Switchyard，一个Apache-2.0的Rust代理和库，用于LLM流量。它将请求解码为供应商中立类型，通过多种算法路由，并转换响应，使Claude Code等工具可在vLLM或NIM上运行。预alpha阶段，不用于生产。

title: Google DeepMind Releases Gemini 3.8 Flash and Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber: One Core Model, Two Access Envelopes
summary: Google released Gemini 3.8 Flash and Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber on September 2, 2026. Both variants run on the same foundational intelligence, split by safety mitigations rather than model size. Gemini 3.8 Flash is generally available at $0.75 and $3.75 per 1M tokens, introductory through December 31, 2026. Flash Cyber reaches 47.2% pass@1 on CWE-Bench and is restricted to vetted defenders through the Fairwind Program. This article covers the benchmarks, the token-for-accuracy tradeoff, and what deploying either one actually requires. The post Google DeepMind Releases Gemini 3.8 Flash and Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber: One Core Model, Two Access Envelopes appeared first on MarkTechPost .

summary_en: Google launches Gemini 3.8 Flash and Flash Cyber, sharing core intelligence but differing in safety. Flash is widely available at $0.75/$3.75 per 1M tokens; Cyber, for vetted defenders, scores 47.2% on CWE-Bench.
summary_zh: 谷歌推出Gemini 3.8 Flash和Flash Cyber，共享核心智能但安全措施不同。Flash广泛可用，价格每百万token 0.75/3.75美元；Cyber面向经审核的防御者，CWE-Bench得分47.2%。
